Interpreting the June 16, 2021 FOMC statement through the New Keynesian/DSGE lens still suggests a systematic, expectations‑anchoring stance: policy rates held at 0–0.25% with average inflation targeting, ongoing balance‑sheet expansion, and floor‑system tools (IOER, ON RRP) preserving accommodative financial conditions while “looking through” transitory inflation. Incorporating the Financial Stability Report (May 2021) tempers this optimism: the FSR highlights elevated asset valuations and strong risk appetite, still‑high business leverage, lingering stress in certain CRE segments, and structural fragilities in short‑term funding markets and liquidity‑mismatch vehicles, even as banks appear resilient and funding conditions have improved. Netting these, the tone remains moderately positive due to growth momentum and policy support, but with clearer caution around financial vulnerabilities and tail risks.
